name: CLOVES Syndrome
aliases: Congenital Lipomatous Overgrowth, Vascular malformations, Epidermal nevi, and Skeletal anomalies syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital, segmental lipomatous overgrowth
Complex vascular malformations including capillary, venous, and lymphatic anomalies
Presence of epidermal nevi or other cutaneous lesions
Skeletal abnormalities such as scoliosis, limb length discrepancy, or macrodactyly
Identification of somatic activating mutation in PIK3CA gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital segmental lipomatous overgrowth and vascular malformations, with or without epidermal nevi or skeletal anomalies; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by genetic testing for PIK3CA mutations; mosaicism may limit detection.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically asymmetric and localized to trunk or limbs
Often combined malformations causing swelling and pain
Linear or patchy hyperpigmented skin lesions

common.symptomName: Skeletal anomalies including scoliosis and limb length discrepancy
Chronic pain related to overgrowth and vascular malformations

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to spinal or nerve compression
occasional.notes: Includes pain, weakness, or sensory changes
Diffuse or localized skin color changes

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular anomalies such as aneurysms or cardiac malformations

laboratory: Possible elevated D-dimer or coagulation abnormalities if vascular malformations complicated
imaging: MRI showing fatty overgrowth and vascular malformations
Ultrasound or Doppler studies of vascular anomalies
genetic: Somatic activating mutations in PIK3CA gene detected by targeted sequencing
other: Histopathology of skin lesions showing epidermal nevi

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive asymmetric overgrowth with cerebriform connective tissue nevi

redFlags: Rapid progression of overgrowth causing functional impairment
Severe vascular malformations with bleeding or thrombosis
Neurological deficits due to nerve or spinal cord compression
references: Keppler-Noreuil KM, Rios JJ, Parker VE, et al. PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS): Diagnostic and Testing Eligibility Criteria, Differential Diagnosis, and Evaluation. Am J Med Genet A. 2015.
Lindhurst MJ, Sapp JC, Teer JK, et al. A mosaic activating mutation in AKT1 associated with the Proteus syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2011.
Alomari AI. CLOVES syndrome: clinical and imaging features. Pediatr Radiol. 2010.
